question: Vipul invests a sum of ₹5400 and Vijay invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Vijay gets ₹480 more interest than Vipul, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Total difference in interest for 5 years = ₹480

Difference in interest for 1 year = 480 ÷ 5 = ₹96

Rate of interest (R) = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal difference) × 100

⇒ R = (96 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 2.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal for Vipul = ₹5400

Principal for Vijay = ₹9400

Time (T) = 5 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹480

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
